content: You are an expert in Geometry Creation and Spatial understanding. You answer short but very precise and including every necessary detail. If you're specifically asked to use functions, use the functions you're supplied and always include all required variables. Don't use those functions unless you were asked to do so. You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

I want to create a toy car model. Create a box with dimensions 200x100x100(X,Y,Z) as the body. The windshield can be created by subtracting a 50x100x50 block from an upper edge of the box. Add four wheels with a radius of 25 and a thickness of 10: Place two at (25,0,0) and (175,0,0) facing in the Y-Axis (0,1,0), and two at (25,100,0) and (175,100,0) facing in the negative Y-Axis (0,-1,0). | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Step-by-step implementation plan (no function execution yet)

1. Create the car body  
   • Call functions.block with one element  
   • Parameters  
     – x_size = [200], y_size = [100], z_size = [100]  
     – x = [0], y = [0], z = [0]      (origin is the left-front-bottom corner)  
     – subtraction = [False]          (first solid establishes the volume)

2. Carve out the windshield opening  
   • Call functions.block with one element for subtraction  
   • Place it on the upper-front edge of the body  
     – x_size = [50], y_size = [100], z_size = [50]  (50 mm long, full width, top half height)  
     – x = [0], y = [0], z = [50]                    (starts flush with front, top half of body)  
     – subtraction = [True]                         (removes material)

3. Add the four wheels (cylinders)  
   • Call functions.cylinder once with four elements filled in the lists

   Base-center coordinates  
     – baseCenterX = [25, 175, 25, 175]  
     – baseCenterY = [ 0,   0, 100, 100]  
     – baseCenterZ = [25,  25,  25,  25]  (wheel centres 25 mm above ground)

   Axis (height) vectors – thickness 10 mm along ±Y  
     – heightVectX = [0, 0, 0, 0]  
     – heightVectY = [10, 10, –10, –10]   (front pair faces +Y, rear pair –Y)  
     – heightVectZ = [0, 0, 0, 0]

   Other parameters  
     – radius = [25, 25, 25, 25]  
     – subtraction = [False, False, False, False]  
     – cylinder_func = [0, 0, 0, 0]        (plain geometry)

4. Finish the model  
   • Call functions.finished with allFunctionsCalled = true after the above calls.

These four calls (block → block (subtract) → cylinder → finished) fully create the toy-car geometry exactly as requested.
